cohort: The study included 78 mother-child binomials in Sao Paulo-SP.
finding: Skin-to-skin contact was performed in nearly all births (94.9%) but often for a shorter duration (mean 29 minutes) than recommended, with various conditions influencing its length and successful breastfeeding attachment.
mod_finding: Births with intact perineum were associated with longer skin-to-skin contact duration and positively influenced breastfeeding attachment.
